text: On the Lorenz task, which NVAR features carry the largest ridge coefficients, and what do they represent?
choices: The constant (bias) term, reflecting the mean of the attractor
The highest-lag linear terms, reflecting very long memory
Random features, since all coefficients end up essentially equal
Quadratic product terms such as x·x, y·y, and x·y, which encode the Lorenz equations' xy and xz nonlinearities
explanation: The lab's feature-importance analysis shows the dominant coefficients on quadratic self/cross products (x·x, y·y, x·y) — precisely the monomials that reproduce the xy and xz terms in the Lorenz RHS. The bias (option 0) and highest-lag linear terms (option 1) carry minor weight, and the coefficients are far from uniform (option 2 is false) — that non-uniformity is exactly what makes NVAR interpretable.
